note: Classification bindings from every reachable input path, one register or SOS variable per claim. Source declarations: SOS Variabelnivå `external_classification` (workbook CLS), FK thin registers and canonical-SCB thin variables with their own lists (`canon`). Label rules: a book's `[binding] value_set_labels` matched against SCB Vardemangder version names (the only adapter that delivers a version label). Overrides: a book's `[[binding.variable]]`. The replaced tests applied hand-built 'declared' curation cases, which no build constructs (only `[[coding.sentinel]]` compiles a classification case); each claim is restated through one of these paths. The old tests cut windows inside 2020 (a Jan-Jun / Jul-Dec split, a Jun-Aug competitor); no build input can narrow a binding inside a coding segment (a label-rule binding takes the segment's window, a declaration or override binding the occurrence's scope, the same scope as that record's code-list claim), so SPLIT restates the relational claim at year grain over 2019-2021: the second book holds only in the middle year and the outer years keep one book. The old missing-coding-period claim is restated for a declaration over 2019-2020 whose code list covers only 2020 (GAP): the coding fold already reports the uncovered year, so the binding neither hides that report nor supplies codes. Books DIG and CNF are bound to no state; they pin how a book's own CSV becomes its codes.
fails_if: `resolve_classification_conformance` (source_classifications.py) waives a nonstandard code when overlap is high (HIGH conforms), matches sentinels by label or by stripped digits (SENTMIX '0' becomes a sentinel), copies the book's labels into the value set (CONF shows 'Canonical label'), counts a code once per label instead of once (DUPLAB's '01' under two labels: `ResolvedConformance` refuses the duplicate checked code and the build stops), or skips a falsy code (BLANKB's '' leaves its nonconforming members, so its conformance row would read conforming without the '' conformance_codes row and warning; the writer's cross-checks in resolved_catalog.py catch the disagreement and the build stops); `_source_bindings` (source_classification_bindings.py) binds a known declaration beside an unresolved one (UNRESURL/UNRESFRAG gain 'fix'), resolves a reference by a fragment of its text, lets a family alias pick an edition that does not cover the whole occurrence (SPANCOL/OVLCOL/NONECOL gain a book), or turns a pooled scope into dated bindings (POOLCOL gains 'fix'); the merge in `apply_classification_cases` picks one winner among plural books (MULTI, CONTRAC or TWOCOL lose one) or stops reporting them as `multiple_classifications_declared`, binds an override without inline codes (NOCODES gains 'two'), keeps a matching rule beside an override (OVR gains 'fix'), or spreads a book bound in one year over its neighbours (SPLIT 2019/2021 gain 'alt'); `_label_rule_bindings` makes one binding per label instead of per book (PAIR gains a second provenance); version names reach rule matching unnormalized (LKF loses 'fix' and 'LKF 1998' goes stale; the SCB adapter's `_clean_descriptor` and `_label_rule_bindings` each normalize, so only dropping both fails it); or `resolve_canonical_codes` keeps a contested book code, splits its label conflict into one issue per competing row (CNF's one `conflicting_classification_labels` issue becomes two) or keys codes after normalization (CNF keeps '1', DIG loses a literal code); or formation or the resolved writer drops a labelled blank code, keys members by code alone, or folds '01' into '1' (MEMBERS loses '' 'Uppgift saknas', one of 01's labels, or 1)
